doc.title: A.B. Spellman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 19, 2022

title: Fascism and the current political moment
summary: His view that proto-fascism is rising in the US and how to oppose it.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: What is your opinion — this strays off a little bit. When historians look back on our current time in the United States do you have any idea what they will say about it?
Yes. About this time and this —

I think they will say that this is a time when fascism took serious hold in the United States. I think that there is a protofascism growing on the right which is absolutely terrifying and it is stronger than anything on the left at this particular moment. And the question is how will all this resolve. I think that there’s such a move, I think Donald Trump introduced such an attitude of authoritarianism and a disregard for institutions or for the laws and rules that had held society together for a while, even with all the contradictions that American society has had within it, and that disregard has taken root in a portion of the country now that makes it all very frightening to me. I think we’re in some serious trouble.
I can’t disagree. I wonder if you have any thoughts about how we get out of it.

Well some of it I don’t have thoughts because a lot of it has to do with the Internet and that I never understood, this electronic age, in a way that gives me a critique of it that would make any sense to anybody. So that part of it no. I think that there has to be more of a unity among people who would oppose this rise of fascism and at least unity on certain principles that this has to be stopped, even if they can’t find unity on where society goes afterwards. But I think now the focus is it should be to stop the rise of this authoritarian right.
Okay. Thanks for addressing that. Back to the music for a moment —
